description: Build the E2E suite - one scenario that fetches a page slug and title from the WordPress REST API and then proves in the browser that the corresponding page renders a matching title, demonstrating API-seeded UI verification - and write the repository README in deliberately basic UK English for a QA engineer new to C# and BDD. Depends on FEAT-002 (PagesClient) and FEAT-003 (page objects, hooks), because the E2E project is the only one that registers both layers.
steps: Create the test project wiring at d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E: reqnroll.json with { "language": { "feature": "en-GB" } }; AssemblyInfo.cs with NO Parallelizable attribute, because E2E runs serially - say so in a comment; CrossLayerContext.cs with ApiSlug, ApiTitle, ApiLink and BrowserTitle; and E2EScenarioDependencies.cs with a static [ScenarioDependencies] factory calling TestConfigurationLoader.Load(), AddTestConfiguration, AddBrowserSupport, AddPageObjects, AddApiClients and registering CrossLayerContext and ScenarioCorrelation scoped. This is the only project that registers both layers.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E\WebDriverHooks.cs with the same shape as the UI project's: ScenarioDriver, FailureArtefacts and ScenarioContext injected; [BeforeScenario(Order = 10)] starting the driver; [AfterScenario(Order = 100)] capturing artefacts when ScenarioContext.TestError is not null and calling ScenarioDriver.Quit() in the finally. Add a comment stating this file is deliberately duplicated rather than shared because project-structure.md forbids a test project referencing another test project, and code-style.md prefers DAMP duplication over a premature abstraction.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E\Features\PublishedPageRendersInBrowser.feature with feature-level tags @e2e @smoke @marketing, a comment explaining this demonstrates API-seeded UI verification - the API decides which page to check and what its title should contain, then the browser proves it renders - and one scenario, 'A page published through the content API renders with a matching title in the browser': Given the content API supplies the page with the configured known slug / When the visitor opens that page in the browser / Then the browser page title mentions the title the content API reported.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E\Steps\PublishedPageRendersInBrowserSteps.cs as async Task bindings, because the Given touches HTTP. The Given calls PagesClient.FindPagesBySlugAsync(SiteOptions.KnownPageSlug, ...) and stores the slug, the title.rendered value and the link into CrossLayerContext. The When makes the synchronous Selenium navigation call plainly on its own line without awaiting it, because it does not return a Task.

Before navigating, guard the When with Core's UrlHostChecker.HasSameHost(SiteOptions.BaseUrl, context.ApiLink) and throw a plain-English exception if the API handed back a different host. Add a comment explaining why: a URL taken from a response is untrusted input, so the suite never navigates to it blindly.

In the Then, assert the browser title CONTAINS the API title case-insensitively, with a because reason, and add a comment explaining the rule: Landmark's titles are SEO titles with no uniform suffix - the API reports 'Technical' while the browser shows 'Technical - Landmark minimum recommended hardware requirements | Landmark Systems' - so equality is not assertable and contains is the real contract.

Write d:\git\QAAutomation\README.md in UK English, deliberately basic, for a QA engineer who may come from manual testing and may be new to C# and BDD. Keep paragraphs short and explain every C# term on first use. Sections in this order: (1) What this is - a template, not a product suite, and the SUT is a public placeholder for KEYinfinity. (2) When to write a UI, an API or an E2E test - a short decision table ending in the rule 'prefer the lowest layer that can prove it'. (3) Directory map - every folder in the tree with one line on what belongs there and one line on where a new test of each kind goes. (4) Prerequisites - the .NET 10 SDK and Google Chrome; state plainly that there is NO browser-driver install step because Selenium Manager, built into Selenium 4.6+, downloads the matching driver on first run, and that the machine therefore needs outbound network access the first time. (5) First run - copy-pasteable PowerShell: cd d:\git\QAAutomation, dotnet restore, dotnet build, dotnet test. (6) Running a subset - one suite (dotnet test tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api), one feature (--filter "FullyQualifiedName~PageListing"), one tag (--filter "TestCategory=smoke"), and how Gherkin tags become NUnit categories. (7) From Gherkin to code - a numbered trace of the real line 'Then the pagination headers report positive whole numbers' through the feature file, PageListingSteps.cs, PagesClient, IWordPressApi and HeaderValueReader, plus a second numbered trace for a UI line through HomepageSteps.cs, HomePage and ElementWaits.

Continue the README with: (8) How do I add a new test? - a numbered recipe: pick the layer, pick or create the .feature file, tag it with one layer tag plus one suite tag plus one feature-area tag, write the Gherkin declaratively, add the binding to the capability's *Steps.cs, add the method to the page object or client, register anything new in that project's *ScenarioDependencies.cs, run the single test, read the artefacts if it fails. (9) House rules, each with a one-line reason - no LINQ (a foreach is readable by anyone and you can breakpoint any line; the build warns, and the upgrade path to Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BannedApiAnalyzers is noted if a harder gate is ever wanted); no Thread.Sleep (Selenium does not auto-wait, so every wait goes through the one ElementWaits helper and a sleep only moves the race); no secrets in the repository (committed config carries YOUR_API_KEY_HERE and real values arrive as QAAUTOMATION_* environment variables, for example $env:QAAUTOMATION_Api__BaseUrl); assertions live in steps, never in page objects or clients (a page object that asserts cannot be reused by a scenario with a different expectation); data-testid becomes the primary locator on KEYinfinity (this template cannot use it because the placeholder site is third-party, which is a deliberate documented exception).

Finish the README with: (10) Honest limitations - the SUT is a public marketing website standing in for KEYinfinity; it is production and READ-ONLY; the contact form is never submitted and ContactUsPage deliberately has no submit method; X-WP-Total is live so no count is ever hard-asserted; the hero carousel and animated counters are never asserted on; CI wiring is parked by the user so there is no pipelines folder; and moving to KEYinfinity means changing Site:BaseUrl and Api:BaseUrl and restoring data-testid as the primary locator. (11) Where failures are recorded - d:\git\QAAutomation\test-results\<suite>\<scenario>-<timestamp>\ with screenshot.png, page-source.html, console.log and location.txt, written on failure only, plus the QAAUTOMATION_Artefacts__Directory override. (12) Glossary - BDD, Gherkin, Given/When/Then, step definition, page object, tag, flaky test, explicit wait, boundary value analysis.
Run every PowerShell command quoted in the README from a fresh shell at d:\git\QAAutomation and correct any that does not work as written.
acceptance_criteria: dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E passes its 1 scenario with 0 failed.
dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\QAAutomation.sln passes all 17 scenarios across the three test projects with 0 failed and 0 skipped.
dotnet build d:\git\QAAutomation\QAAutomation.sln reports 0 Warning(s) and 0 Error(s).
README.md contains all twelve named sections, and every PowerShell command quoted in it runs successfully when pasted into a fresh shell at the repository root.

README.md states explicitly that there is no browser-driver install step, that Chrome must be installed, that the contact form is never submitted, and that live content counts are never hard-asserted.
After the E2E run, Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue returns nothing.
verification: Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue - must return nothing after the run
Paste each PowerShell command block from README.md into a fresh shell at d:\git\QAAutomation and confirm each succeeds
findings:
SCENARIO COUNT IS 18, NOT 17 - CONFIRMED, AND THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS WRONG RATHER THAN THE SUITE. FEAT-002 already recorded this: PageListing.feature is 3 plain scenarios plus two Scenario Outlines of 2 rows each (7 test cases) and PageLookup.feature is 2, so the API suite is 9 test cases, not 8. With 8 UI and 1 E2E, 'dotnet test QAAutomation.sln' reports 9 + 8 + 1 = 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Nothing was added or split to reach that number - the planned scenario set was built exactly as FEAT-002/003/004 specify, and 17 was an arithmetic slip in plan.md item 10. Every other part of the criterion (0 failed, 0 skipped, all three projects) holds. The README states 18, because a README that disagrees with the runner is worse than no README.

SURPRISE 1 - LandedPage HAD NO WAY TO OPEN AN ARBITRARY ADDRESS, SO FEAT-003's FILE HAD TO CHANGE. FEAT-003 flagged this and it is the one edit outside tests/QAAutomation.Tests.E2E. src/QAAutomation.UI/Pages/LandedPage.cs gained Open(string url) - three lines plus a guard clause that throws ArgumentException on a blank address, and a 'using System;' for it. The host check deliberately did NOT go in there: the plan puts UrlHostChecker.HasSameHost in the When, and a page object navigates where it is told while deciding whether an address is trustworthy belongs to the caller. The method's comment says so, and says no wait is done there because what counts as 'loaded' depends on what the scenario is about to check (the Then waits for the title it is about to read, through ElementWaits.WaitUntilTitleContains).

SURPRISE 2 - AN AssemblyInfo.cs WITH NO Parallelizable ATTRIBUTE MUST ALSO HAVE NO 'using'. The UI copy starts with 'using NUnit.Framework;' because it carries NUnit attributes. The E2E copy carries none, so that using would be unused - and FEAT-001 turned GenerateDocumentationFile on, which makes IDE0005 (unused using) a REAL BUILD WARNING. tests/QAAutomation.Tests.E2E/AssemblyInfo.cs is therefore comments only, zero code, and the build stays at 0 Warning(s). Anyone adding a Parallelizable attribute later must add the using back at the same time.

SURPRISE 3 - ScenarioCorrelation MUST NOT BE REGISTERED IN THE E2E FACTORY. FEAT-004 step 1 lists it, but AddBrowserSupport() already registers it scoped (FEAT-001's CoreRegistration), and AddApiClients' RequestContextHandler only needs it to exist. Registering it again would be a duplicate line that silently shadows the first. E2EScenarioDependencies therefore calls AddTestConfiguration, AddBrowserSupport, AddPageObjects, AddApiClients(testConfiguration.Api) and registers ONLY CrossLayerContext scoped, with a comment explaining that ScenarioCorrelation arrives with AddBrowserSupport and that the API test project has to register it itself because it has no browser support. The intent of the step is met - it IS registered scoped - without the duplication. Verified by the suite passing: the correlation header handler resolves and the request goes out.

SURPRISE 4 - THE GENERATED FIXTURE NAME FOR THIS FEATURE IS PublishedPageRendersInTheBrowserFeature. The feature title is 'Published page renders in the browser', and Reqnroll names the class from the TITLE, not the file name (PublishedPageRendersInBrowser.feature). So '--filter "FullyQualifiedName~PublishedPageRendersInBrowser"' matches nothing. This is FEAT-003's surprise 4 recurring, and it is why the README's 'running a subset' section calls the trap out explicitly and lists all six generated names: PageListingFeature, PageLookupFeature, HomePageFeature, PrimaryNavigationFeature, EnquiryFormFeature, PublishedPageRendersInTheBrowserFeature. Verified by running the filter: 'FullyQualifiedName~PageListingFeature' returns 7 test cases.

ASSERTION USED FOR THE CROSS-LAYER TITLE RULE. AwesomeAssertions 9.6.0 has ContainEquivalentOf(string, because) for case-insensitive string containment, which is exactly the cross_layer_title_rule: the API reports 'Technical' and the browser shows 'Technical - Landmark minimum recommended hardware requirements | Landmark Systems'. It compiles and passes with no extra configuration. ElementWaits.WaitUntilTitleContains is already case-insensitive (StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), so the wait and the assertion agree on casing. The reason string names the business rule, and a long comment above it explains why equality is not assertable - there is no uniform suffix, each page's SEO title is hand-written - so nobody 'tightens' it to Should().Be() later.

README - WHAT CHANGED BECAUSE OF ACTUALLY PASTING THE COMMANDS. Every PowerShell block was run in a fresh shell at d:/git/QAAutomation. Four were written defensively BECAUSE a naive version fails or is harmful when pasted:
1. The artefact listing is wrapped in 'if (Test-Path test-results) { ... } else { "No failures recorded." }'. A bare Get-ChildItem test-results errors on a green run, and a green run writing nothing is the normal healthy state - so the defensive form also teaches the right thing. Observed output: 'No failures recorded.'
2. Both environment-variable examples are SET-then-Remove-Item pairs with no 'dotnet test' between them. Pasting a bare '$env:QAAUTOMATION_Api__BaseUrl = ...' would leave the override in the reader's shell and silently change every later run - the worst kind of documentation side effect. The pair is harmless to paste and still shows the pattern.
3. 'Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' sets $? to False when nothing matches (a silenced non-terminating error). It prints nothing, throws nothing and the shell carries on, which is what the README promises and what the acceptance criterion asks for. Without -ErrorAction it writes a red error on a healthy machine.
4. The Chrome prerequisite check is 'Test-Path "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe"', which returns True or False and always succeeds. 'Get-Command chrome' is not reliable - Chrome is not on PATH. Observed: True, alongside 'dotnet --list-sdks' showing 10.0.301 and 8.0.425.
The section 5 block (cd, dotnet restore, dotnet build, dotnet test) was run with no explicit solution path and resolves QAAutomation.sln correctly - there is no leftover .slnx to make that ambiguous.

FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED - OUTSIDE FEAT-004's STEPS. The Reqnroll generator emits *.feature.cs NEXT TO the .feature file (tests/*/Features/*.feature.cs), not into obj/ as context.json states. .gitignore does not list them, and this workspace is not a git repository so nothing was committed either way. The README's directory map tells the reader those files are generated and must never be edited or committed. If git is ever initialised here, add '*.feature.cs' to .gitignore - that is a one-line change and it belongs to FEAT-005's integration pass, not here.

STEERING COMPLIANCE. No LINQ: a scan of the new E2E files and LandedPage.cs for 'using System.Linq', '.Where(', '.Select(', 'FirstOrDefault', '.Any(', '.All(' returns nothing. No Thread.Sleep, no .Result, no .Wait(), no GetAwaiter, no async void. No By, FindElement or WebDriverWait in any step file - the only wait is ElementWaits.WaitUntilTitleContains, called from the Then. Explicit types throughout, no ternary, no null-conditional chain. The Given is async Task because it makes an HTTP call; the When is a plain void method because Selenium is synchronous and the navigation call sits on its own line with no await. The Given asserts nothing and throws InvalidOperationException with a plain-English message if the API returns no page for the configured slug, because a precondition that cannot be met is a set-up error. The host guard is a guard clause, not an assertion, and says so in a comment. WebDriverHooks.cs and ContainerStartup.cs are deliberate verbatim copies of the UI suite's (SuiteName 'e2e' is the only behavioural difference) and both carry a comment naming the two rules that force the duplication: project-structure.md forbids a test project referencing another, and code-style.md prefers DAMP duplication over a premature abstraction. No steering file was edited - FEAT-004 needed no new package pin (the E2E csproj already had the full package set from FEAT-001) and no new tag (@e2e, @smoke and @marketing were all already in the taxonomy). No secret, key or token appears in any new file; appsettings.json was not touched.

VERIFICATION OUTPUT OBSERVED, FEAT-004's FIVE COMMANDS RUN AS WRITTEN.
1. 'dotnet build d:\\git\\QAAutomation\\QAAutomation.sln' -> 'Build succeeded.' / '0 Warning(s)' / '0 Error(s)'.
2. 'dotnet test d:\\git\\QAAutomation\\tests\\QAAutomation.Tests.E2E' -> 'Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 1, Skipped: 0, Total: 1'. The step trace printed Given 1.3s, When 5.1s, Then 0.1s, so the browser hand-off works and the title wait returns immediately rather than burning its timeout.
3. 'dotnet test d:\\git\\QAAutomation\\QAAutomation.sln' -> three 'Passed!' lines: Api 9/9, E2E 1/1, UI 8/8. 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Run three times in total (once inside the README's section 5 block from a fresh shell), green every time.
4. 'Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' -> nothing, after every run including the three-suite runs. Teardown quits the driver.
5. Every PowerShell block in README.md pasted into a fresh shell at d:/git/QAAutomation: all succeed. Subset commands verified individually - 'dotnet test tests\\QAAutomation.Tests.Api' 9 passed, '--filter "FullyQualifiedName~PageListingFeature"' 7 passed, 'dotnet test tests\\QAAutomation.Tests.UI --filter "TestCategory=smoke"' 1 passed.
Also confirmed: test-results/ does not exist after a green run, so nothing is written on pass; README.md contains all twelve numbered sections in the specified order; and the README states explicitly that there is no browser-driver install step (section 4, with the Selenium Manager reason and the outbound-access consequence), that Chrome must be installed (section 4), that the contact form is never submitted and ContactUsPage has no submit method (section 10), and that no test asserts a live content count with the full reason why (section 10).

NOT DONE, AS INSTRUCTED: no git anything - the workspace is not a repository, so nothing was initialised, branched, committed or pushed. No pipelines/ folder. Nothing in .kiro was edited. FEAT-005's final integration audit (the repository-wide grep for FluentAssertions, ChromeDriver, WebDriverManager, DotNetSeleniumExtras and the leftover-file sweep) was not run - that is its own feature.
